newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA TELECOMS-Telstra may become electronic broker.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA TELECOMS-Telstra may become electronic broker.

text.p: Australian state-owned telecom Telstra Corp may become a kind of electronic broker once it launches its huge Yellow Pages telephone directory into the world of on-line commerce through its broadband network.

Telstra Multimedia chief executive Gerry Moriarty told Reuters the group was working on an on-line interactive version of the huge business directory, which lists around 300,000 paying advertisers nation-wide.
"We are seeing some very early versions on that at the present time. We are prividing enhanced electronic ads or entries for some of our customers now," Moriarty said.

He described Yellow Pages as Australia's premier electronic trading forum of the future, with shoppers browsing, ordering and paying for goods and services via a Yellow Pages virtual-reality shopping mall.
"We own that content and we have the business relationship with all of those customers -- that is, every business in Australia has a listing in the Yellow Pages," Moriarty said.
"They might not all have an advertisement, but they all have a listing, so we have a business relationship with every one of them," he said.
Telstra may continue to charge for advertising space on the on-line Yellow Pages but transaction fees on cyberspace trading represent some of the biggest revenue potential, he said.
"The way in which revenue will be derived increasingly in the future will be on a per-transaction basis," Moriarty said.

"Now whether that transaction is just buying a further piece of information ... or a financial transaction where someone is buying a commodity ... (this) is where we all see the opportunity for revenues," he said.
Yellow Pages, which has taken its first step into cyberspace by launching a relatively passive site on the Internet, is run by Pacific Access Pty Ltd, which is half owned by Telstra.
The rest is split equally among U.S. firms South Western Bell and Volt Information Sciences Inc, and Bell Canada and Australian firm Edward O'Brien Industries.
Australia's richest single publishing asset, Yellow Pages has annual turnover approaching A$1 billion, Moriarty said.
"There's huge opportunity to grow that area in terms of enhancements and so forth," he said.
"On the other hand, one recognises that people, particularly in electronic services, have an expectation that information services are going to be relatively cheap."
The Yellow Pages on-line shopping mall will be launched after the unveiling later this year of an electronic payments system developed by Telstra in conjunction with some banks.
The payments system will enable Telstra customers to do business via the Internet, closed on-line systems and even via the normal copper-wire telephone network, Moriarty said.
